additions.reason: The Rebbe uses the phrase 'קטנות ופגם באמונה' in line 4 as a bechina-level description of the same condition as קטני אמנה / קצר רוח. He writes: 'כמוכן כשיש קטנות ופגם באמונה, צריכין לעשות עבודות קשות' — directly parallel to 'מחמת שהם קטני אמנה.' This phrase names the inner spiritual impairment that constitutes being a קטן אמנה: it is a diminishment (קטנות) and flaw (פגם) in one's faith. While this is closely synonymous with קטני אמנה, it is a distinct formulation that highlights the qualitative impairment aspect. It belongs in Package 2 alongside קטני אמנה and קצר רוח as a further elaboration of the same deficient state.
additions.source_quote: כְּמוֹ כֵן כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ קַטְנוּת וּפְגָם בֶּאֱמוּנָה, צְרִיכִין לַעֲשׂוֹת עֲבוֹדוֹת קָשׁוֹת

additions.reason: The Rebbe uses 'קלקול אמונה לגמרי' (complete ruin of faith) in line 4 to describe the condition of שעת שמד — the state analogous to, but more extreme than, קטני אמנה. He writes: 'כמו שבשעת השמד שהיא קלקול אמונה לגמרי.' This phrase describes the total destruction of faith, which is parallel to Package 3 (עבודה זרה והכפירות = אין יש רוח בהם). It belongs in Package 3 as an alternative name for the total-absence-of-emunah state: complete ruin of faith is equivalent to the heresy/idolatry condition where there is no ruach at all. This is a bechina equivalence — both describe the same extreme state: the soul in which faith has been entirely destroyed.

analysis_notes.coverage_assessment: The dataset for Torah LM2/86 is sparse but accurate. All three bechina equatings from the source text are captured. The text is unusually short (5 lines) and presents a single clean argument: the ruach/emunah spectrum. The two additional nodes proposed above (קטנות ופגם באמונה and קלקול אמונה) are bechina-level equivalents found in the source text that would enrich the dataset.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_structure: This Torah presents a three-level mirror on a single axis — the ruach/emunah dimension: (1) Complete faith = long spirit [good]; (2) Little faith = short spirit [intermediate/failing]; (3) Heresy/idolatry = no spirit at all [evil]. The good/evil mirror is clean: Package 1 and Package 3 are the two poles of the same axis (one = the fullness of ruach-emunah, the other = its total absence). Package 2 is the middle zone — the Torah's primary practical concern — which the Rebbe addresses with the prescription of harsh avodah as a corrective measure.
analysis_notes.note_on_shemad_analogy: The concept of 'שעת שמד' (time of religious persecution) appears prominently in the text as a structural analogy but is used in an eitza/mashal (analogical) capacity, not as a bechina node in its own right. The Rebbe argues: just as during a shemad even trivial violations require martyrdom, so too any deficiency in faith requires proportionally harder spiritual effort. This is not a bechina equivalence between shemad and קטני אמנה — it is an argument about parallel responses to parallel levels of faith-danger.
analysis_notes.note_on_צדיקים: Line 5 notes that even tzaddikim (righteous people) can be in the state of קטני אמנה, citing Sotah 48b on 'כי מי בז ליום קטנות.' The word 'צדיקים' here is mentioned as an example of who can be in Package 2, not as a new bechina node — so no new node is proposed.
